# SB-1022 Safety bulletin: stored hydraulic energy

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01

Hazard description
Stored hydraulic energy in press and shot blast auxiliary systems presents a latent release hazard during maintenance, inspection, and tooling changes. Residual pressure trapped in hydraulic accumulators, hoses, cylinders, valves, and cylinder end caps can cause sudden actuator movement, high-velocity fluid discharge, or component separation when a restraint is removed or a fitting is loosened. In the shot blast cabinet environment, hydraulic release can inject particulate into the workspace, displace guarding, or create slip hazards when hydraulic lubricant reaches floor surfaces. Stored energy incidents can occur without obvious external indications because system gauges may show no pressure or because mechanical locks mask internal spring preloads or trapped charge.

Background and rationale
This bulletin addresses EQ-P3-L3-SB01, a machining shot blast cabinet that integrates hydraulic components for door actuation and auxiliary tool positioning. The presence of stored hydraulic energy is a common industrial risk that has led to injuries at other facilities when procedures do not explicitly verify zero energy or use positive isolation methods. Eliminating or controlling stored energy is a basic safety principle aligned with lockout/tagout best practices.

The lubricant part number for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is CFW-LUB-709. Knowledge of the correct lubricant is required for contamination control and for maintenance steps that involve fluid handling. Use of the specified lubricant prevents incompatibilities that could alter seal behavior and affect the reliability of pressure-retaining components.

Affected equipment
- EQ-P3-L3-SB01 (Machining shot blast cabinet #1) and all connected hydraulic lines, accumulators, cylinders, valves, quick disconnects, and end fittings located on line P3-L3.  
- Any portable hydraulic test equipment temporarily connected during troubleshooting or maintenance.  
- Local guarding, sensors, and interlocks that rely on hydraulic positioners for safe function.

Required controls
Administrative controls
- Work on any hydraulic component on EQ-P3-L3-SB01 must be planned and authorized by maintenance supervision and documented in the maintenance work record. Refer to SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-03 for procedure steps related to isolation and task-specific permits. Citation: SOP-P3-L3-02; SOP-P3-L3-03.
- A job safety brief must be held before starting any activity that could expose personnel to stored hydraulic energy. The brief must identify potential trapped energy sources, planned isolation points, and rescue communications.
- Use the maintenance manual and schematic for EQ-P3-L3-SB01 for identification of isolation valves and accumulator locations. Citation: MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2.

Isolation and verification
- Before any disassembly or exposure of hydraulic fittings, isolate energy sources using positive physical isolation methods described in SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-03. Where applicable, follow the isolation sequence in MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2.
- Establish a verified zero-energy state by venting residual fluid to a dedicated recovery container and by cycling actuators to their defined safe positions. Verification shall include a physical attempt to move the isolated component using the manual override method described in SOP-P3-L3-03. If motion occurs, re-evaluate isolation.
- Tag and lock isolation points per site lockout/tagout requirements until the work scope is complete and the responsible maintenance technician releases the lock.

Engineering controls
- Where practical, install manual bleed valves or lockable mechanical stops that allow positive mechanical blocking in addition to hydraulic isolation. Use of lockable mechanical stops reduces reliance on hydraulic seals to maintain a safe condition.
- Inspect quick-disconnect fittings and hose assemblies for rated condition prior to reconnecting after maintenance. Replace suspect components with approved parts in the maintenance inventory that reference MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2 for compatibility.

Personal protective equipment and work practices
- Required PPE for work involving potential hydraulic fluid release includes splash-resistant eye protection, fluid-resistant gloves, and footwear with slip-resistant soles. Avoid skin contact with hydraulic fluid; wash exposed skin promptly and document exposure events in the safety log.
- Never loosen hydraulic fittings while system pressure status is unknown or while the system has not been isolated and verified to be at zero energy.

Examples and illustrative scenarios
- Example scenario A: A technician plans to remove a door cylinder. Following the administrative controls above, the technician isolates the hydraulic supply, vents the line into a recovery container, applies a mechanical stop to the door, and uses the verification step in SOP-P3-L3-03 to ensure the cylinder cannot move before loosening fittings. This prevents accidental door closure and fluid spray.
- Example scenario B: A faulted quick-disconnect is suspected of leaking. The technician uses MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2 to locate the isolation valve upstream, tags and locks the valve, bleeds residual fluid to the recovery container, and then replaces the fitting with a unit from approved parts. The lubricant specified for EQ-P3-L3-SB01, CFW-LUB-709, is applied at reassembly to the connection as required by the maintenance checklist.

Records to keep
- A maintenance work record must be completed for every intervention that involves hydraulic components on EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Records shall reference the performed isolation steps, verification actions, the personnel who executed lockout/tagout, and the related document citations: MM-P3-L3-SB01-S2; SOP-P3-L3-02; SOP-P3-L3-03.
- PPE inspection notes, any contamination cleanup logs, and incident or near-miss reports related to stored hydraulic energy must be filed with the maintenance supervisor and retained in the plant safety folder for review.
- Lubricant usage records for EQ-P3-L3-SB01 shall note the part number CFW-LUB-709 and be entered into the lubrication log.

Effective date
Effective date: See issuance record held in the document control system.
